# HubRisk — Weather Risk Intelligence Agent

A conversational agent that helps a US logistics company decide which regional distribution hubs are most exposed
to weather disruption. Every number comes from deterministic code over public weather data; the LLM interprets the
question, calls typed tools and explains the result inside an enforced JSON schema.

Design: [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md). Product docs and specs: [agent-os/](agent-os/). The full AI session
used to build this is exported under `docs/ai-session/`.

## Run it

Requires Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```bash
uv sync
uv run agent chat --test "What can you help me with?"   # offline, no key, no spend
uv run agent serve --test                                # http://localhost:8000
```

With real models, copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set at least one vendor key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` recommended;
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` optional). A model whose key is
missing is skipped at startup. Then:

```bash
uv run agent serve                       # chat page at /, API at /api/chat, docs at /api/docs
uv run agent eval --repeat 3 --tag latest
uv run agent eval --down anthropic --tag anthropic-outage   # proves cross-vendor fallback
```

Tests and lint (offline, no keys):

```bash
uv run ruff check src tests
uv run pytest -q
```

## API

- `GET /health` — version, model chain, guard.
- `POST /api/chat` `{"message": "...", "session_id": "optional"}` → the answer plus `status`, `sources`,
  `limitations`, `served_by`, `failed_attempts`, `tools_used`, cost and latency.
- `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` — forget a conversation.
- `GET /api/stats` — budget cap, month-to-date spend and recent calls (Bearer `ADMIN_TOKEN`).

## Spend limits (both are required)

1. In code: `BUDGET_USD` monthly cap enforced by the SQLite ledger before every paid call, plus a per-turn cost
   limit and request limit, 20 requests per IP per hour and 200 per day.
2. In each provider console: the same monthly cap (Anthropic Console → Limits; OpenAI → Billing limits; Google
   Cloud budget). The code refuses before a call; the provider refuses regardless of the code.

## Assumptions, uncertainty and scoping

Filled in by the hubs, scoring and agent specs (v1–v3). See `agent-os/product/mission.md` for the current
scope statement.

## Deployment

Render Blueprint in `render.yaml`. Filled in with the live URL and verification date by the deploy spec (v4).

# HubRisk — Design

Weather disruption risk agent for a US logistics company's regional distribution hubs. This document covers the
system architecture, the repository structure and the data storage choice. Product goals live in
`agent-os/product/`, behaviour in `agent-os/specs/`, conventions in `agent-os/standards/`.

## System architecture

```
browser chat page ──HTTP──▶ FastAPI (app/api)
                               │  rate limit per IP + global, session store (TTL + LRU, one lock per session)
                               ▼
                           Service.ask (app/agent/core.py)
                               │ 1. regex input checks            (app/decide/guard.py, free)
                               │ 2. budget.reserve                (app/llm/budget.py, SQLite ledger)
                               │ 3. guard.screen → Screening      (TypeSafe Jev → Claude Haiku fallback)
                               │ 4. Agent.run(output_type=AnswerOut, UsageLimits)
                               │       └─ FallbackModel chain: Sonnet → Haiku → GPT → Gemini
                               │       └─ FunctionToolset: deterministic tools (hubs, scoring, live weather)
                               │ 5. budget.settle(real cost)
                               ▼
                           Turn (status, answer, sources, limitations, served_by, failed_attempts, cost, latency)
```

- **The LLM never produces a number.** Tools return typed Pydantic models; the model picks tools and explains.
  `AnswerOut` is enforced by Pydantic AI; a reply that fails validation is retried once, then the turn fails loudly.
- **Three retry layers, one job each:** the httpx transport retries 429/5xx/network per model with Retry-After;
  vendor SDK retries are off; `FallbackModel` moves to the next model on an API error or a truncated reply.
  All models down → `status: unavailable`, never a crash.
- **Guard before spend:** the regex layer costs nothing; the decision model is Jev (typed questions, calibrated
  confidence) with Haiku taking over below `guard_confidence` or on error. Refusals are fixed strings and release
  the budget reservation. In `MODEL_MODE=test` the guard is a keyword heuristic (`offline_guard_model`), a test
  double so smoke evals can distinguish in-scope from off-topic offline.
- **Spend is bounded twice:** the ledger enforces `BUDGET_USD` per month before every paid call (reserve →
  settle / release), plus `UsageLimits` per turn and per-IP / daily request limits. Provider consoles carry the
  same cap as the hard backstop.
- **Evals are the quality gate:** `evals/cases.yaml` by category, `agent eval` writes `evals/results/<tag>`,
  exit 0 pass / 1 fail / 2 flaky, `--down <vendor>` proves cross-vendor fallback end to end.

Domain layers (v1–v3): `app/data` (hub registry, Open-Meteo history ingest, NWS live client, DuckDB store),
`app/scoring` (disruption days per year per hazard, uncertainty band, trend, weighted score), domain tools and
prompts in `app/agent`.

## Repository structure

```
config/        agent.yaml (models, limits), prices.yaml (fallback prices), hubs.yaml + scoring.yaml (v1/v2)
src/app/
  config.py    Settings (env) + YAML config loaders
  cli.py       Typer: agent serve | chat | eval | ingest; compose() is the only composition root
  llm/         models.py (chain, retries, fallback), budget.py (SQLite ledger)
  decide/      guard.py (regex layer, Screening, Jev→Haiku, offline guard)
  agent/       schema.py (AnswerOut, Turn), prompts.py, tools.py, core.py (Service)
  api/         app.py (routes), ratelimit.py, sessions.py, static/index.html (chat page)
  evals/       cases.py, runner.py, report.py
  data/        v1: hub registry, weather clients, ingest, DuckDB store
  scoring/     v2: deterministic KPI engine
data/          snapshots/*.parquet committed (v1); runtime SQLite ledger ignored
evals/         cases.yaml, results/<tag>.{json,md}
tests/         offline pytest; test_<spec-slug>.py holds that spec's criterion tests; test_spec_coverage.py enforces
agent-os/      product docs, standards (+ index.yml), one spec folder per version
docs/          this file, ai-session/ (the full agent session transcript, a deliverable)
.github/       CI: ruff + pytest + offline eval smoke
render.yaml    Render Blueprint (python runtime, uv sync --frozen --no-dev, /health probe)
```

## Data storage choice

- **History: DuckDB over Parquet snapshots committed to the repo** (v1). Open-Meteo daily history for all hubs,
  2016–2025, is ingested once locally and committed as Parquet. Rationale: the dataset is small (15 hubs × ~3,650
  days), read-only at runtime, and queried analytically (thresholds, group-by year); DuckDB runs in-process with
  no server and reads Parquet directly; a deploy needs no re-ingest, so Render's ephemeral disk is irrelevant and
  the live demo cannot be broken by an upstream outage. Trade-off: history is frozen at ingest time; refreshing
  is a re-run of `agent ingest` and a commit.
- **Live conditions: not stored.** NWS alerts and forecast are fetched per request with a 10-minute in-memory
  cache; they are a "right now" signal shown beside the historical score, never blended into it.
- **Spend ledger: SQLite at runtime** (`DB_PATH`). Transactional (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) so concurrent turns cannot
  overspend. On Render's free tier the file is ephemeral and resets on redeploy; provider-side limits are the
  backstop and the README says so.
- **Sessions: in memory** (1 h TTL, LRU 500). A restart forgets conversations; acceptable for an analyst tool
  at this scale and stated in the README.

## Trade-offs and known limits

- Thresholds are plausible operational limits, not calibrated to real outage data (none available).
- Reanalysis data is a point at the hub coordinate, not the facility footprint.
- Ten years is short for rare hazards (hurricanes); the year-to-year band is the honest uncertainty we can show.
- Single process, single region, no auth: scoped for a live demo and a small analyst team.

# Shape Spec

Gather context and structure planning for significant work. **Run this command while in plan mode.**

## Important Guidelines

- **Always use AskUserQuestion tool** when asking the user anything
- **Offer suggestions** — Present options the user can confirm, adjust, or correct
- **Keep it lightweight** — This is shaping, not exhaustive documentation

## Prerequisites

This command **must be run in plan mode**.

**Before proceeding, check if you are currently in plan mode.**

If NOT in plan mode, **stop immediately** and tell the user:

```
Shape-spec must be run in plan mode. Please enter plan mode first, then run /shape-spec again.
```

Do not proceed with any steps below until confirmed to be in plan mode.

## Process

### Step 1: Clarify What We're Building

Use AskUserQuestion to understand the scope:

```
What are we building? Please describe the feature or change.

(Be as specific as you like — I'll ask follow-up questions if needed)
```

Based on their response, ask 1-2 clarifying questions if the scope is unclear. Examples:
- "Is this a new feature or a change to existing functionality?"
- "What's the expected outcome when this is done?"
- "Are there any constraints or requirements I should know about?"

### Step 2: Gather Visuals

Use AskUserQuestion:

```
Do you have any visuals to reference?

- Mockups or wireframes
- Screenshots of similar features
- Examples from other apps

(Paste images, share file paths, or say "none")
```

If visuals are provided, note them for inclusion in the spec folder.

### Step 3: Identify Reference Implementations

Use AskUserQuestion:

```
Is there similar code in this codebase I should reference?

Examples:
- "The comments feature is similar to what we're building"
- "Look at how src/features/notifications/ handles real-time updates"
- "No existing references"

(Point me to files, folders, or features to study)
```

If references are provided, read and analyze them to inform the plan.

### Step 4: Check Product Context

Check if `agent-os/product/` exists and contains files.

If it exists, read key files (like `mission.md`, `roadmap.md`, `tech-stack.md`) and use AskUserQuestion:

```
I found product context in agent-os/product/. Should this feature align with any specific product goals or constraints?

Key points from your product docs:
- [summarize relevant points]

(Confirm alignment or note any adjustments)
```

If no product folder exists, skip this step.

### Step 5: Surface Relevant Standards

Read `agent-os/standards/index.yml` to identify relevant standards based on the feature being built.

Use AskUserQuestion to confirm:

```
Based on what we're building, these standards may apply:

1. **api/response-format** — API response envelope structure
2. **api/error-handling** — Error codes and exception handling
3. **database/migrations** — Migration patterns

Should I include these in the spec? (yes / adjust: remove 3, add frontend/forms)
```

Read the confirmed standards files to include their content in the plan context.

### Step 6: Generate Spec Folder Name

Create a folder name using this format:
```
YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-{feature-slug}/
```

Where:
- Date/time is current timestamp
- Feature slug is derived from the feature description (lowercase, hyphens, max 40 chars)

Example: `2026-01-15-1430-user-comment-system/`

**Note:** If `agent-os/specs/` doesn't exist, create it when saving the spec folder.

### Step 7: Structure the Plan

Now build the plan with **Task 1 always being "Save spec documentation"**.

Present this structure to the user:

```
Here's the plan structure. Task 1 saves all our shaping work before implementation begins.

---

## Task 1: Save Spec Documentation

Create `agent-os/specs/{folder-name}/` with:

- **plan.md** — This full plan
- **shape.md** — Shaping notes (scope, decisions, context from our conversation)
- **standards.md** — Relevant standards that apply to this work
- **references.md** — Pointers to reference implementations studied
- **visuals/** — Any mockups or screenshots provided

## Task 2: [First implementation task]

[Description based on the feature]

## Task 3: [Next task]

...

---

Does this plan structure look right? I'll fill in the implementation tasks next.
```

### Step 8: Complete the Plan

After Task 1 is confirmed, continue building out the remaining implementation tasks based on:
- The feature scope from Step 1
- Patterns from reference implementations (Step 3)
- Constraints from standards (Step 5)

Each task should be specific and actionable.

### Step 9: Ready for Execution

When the full plan is ready:

```
Plan complete. When you approve and execute:

1. Task 1 will save all spec documentation first
2. Then implementation tasks will proceed

Ready to start? (approve / adjust)
```

## Output Structure

The spec folder will contain:

```
agent-os/specs/{YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-feature-slug}/
├── plan.md           # The full plan
├── shape.md          # Shaping decisions and context
├── standards.md      # Which standards apply and key points
├── references.md     # Pointers to similar code
└── visuals/          # Mockups, screenshots (if any)
```

## shape.md Content

The shape.md file should capture:

```markdown
# {Feature Name} — Shaping Notes

## Scope

[What we're building, from Step 1]

## Decisions

- [Key decisions made during shaping]
- [Constraints or requirements noted]

## Context

- **Visuals:** [List of visuals provided, or "None"]
- **References:** [Code references studied]
- **Product alignment:** [Notes from product context, or "N/A"]

## Standards Applied

- api/response-format — [why it applies]
- api/error-handling — [why it applies]
```

## standards.md Content

Include the full content of each relevant standard:

```markdown
# Standards for {Feature Name}

The following standards apply to this work.

---

## api/response-format

[Full content of the standard file]

---

## api/error-handling

[Full content of the standard file]
```

## references.md Content

```markdown
# References for {Feature Name}

## Similar Implementations

### {Reference 1 name}

- **Location:** `src/features/comments/`
- **Relevance:** [Why this is relevant]
- **Key patterns:** [What to borrow from this]

### {Reference 2 name}

...
```

## Tips

- **Keep shaping fast** — Don't over-document. Capture enough to start, refine as you build.
- **Visuals are optional** — Not every feature needs mockups.
- **Standards guide, not dictate** — They inform the plan but aren't always mandatory.
- **Specs are discoverable** — Months later, someone can find this spec and understand what was built and why.

"""Tools the model may call. Every tool is deterministic code; the model only chooses and explains.

The v3 agent spec replaces `about` with the domain tools. Keep them pure functions over `ToolContext` so tests
can run them without a model.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic_ai import RunContext
from pydantic_ai.toolsets import FunctionToolset

from app import __version__
from app.agent.prompts import SCOPE_DESCRIPTION


@dataclass
class ToolContext:
    """Everything tools need (DB handles, config). Built once at startup, injected per run as `deps`."""

    product_name: str


class About(BaseModel):
    product: str
    version: str
    scope: str


def about(ctx: RunContext[ToolContext]) -> About:
    """What this assistant is and what it covers. Call when the user asks what you can do."""
    return About(product=ctx.deps.product_name, version=__version__, scope=SCOPE_DESCRIPTION)


def build_toolset() -> FunctionToolset[ToolContext]:
    toolset: FunctionToolset[ToolContext] = FunctionToolset()
    toolset.add_function(about)
    return toolset

    uvicorn.run(web, host=host, port=port or app.settings.port)

    """One question, or an interactive loop when none is given."""
    app = compose(model_mode="test" if test else None)
    conv = Conversation(max_turns=app.config.limits.max_turns)

    async def one(q: str) -> None:
        turn = await app.service.ask(conv, q)
        meta = [turn.status, turn.served_by or turn.guardrail or "", f"{turn.cost_usd:.4f} USD", f"{turn.latency_ms} ms"]
        if turn.failed_attempts:
            meta.append("fallback after " + ", ".join(turn.failed_attempts))
        typer.echo(turn.answer)
        typer.secho(" · ".join(m for m in meta if m), fg="bright_black")

    if question:
        asyncio.run(one(" ".join(question)))
        return
    typer.echo("Interactive chat; empty line to quit.")
    while True:
        try:
            q = input("> ").strip()
        except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
            break
        if not q:
            break
        asyncio.run(one(q))

The NWS API at api.weather.gov is keyless, and it asks clients to send a User-Agent that identifies them. The official NWS documentation confirms the alerts and forecast endpoints, and the rest comes from third-party sources.

**Active alerts for a point.** Use `/alerts/active?point=lat,lon`. One third-party example uses `point=38.8894,-77.0352` with a `User-Agent: (myapp.com, me@myapp.com)` header ([publicapis.io](https://publicapis.io/blog/national-weather-service-api-omuv)). The official NWS docs describe `/alerts/active` as a common-request endpoint that filters by state, such as `?area=KS`, and note that it internally redirects to `/alerts` with `active=true` ([weather.gov](https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-API)). Alerts come back in CAP format, with fields like severity, urgency, event, and expiry ([publicapis.io](https://publicapis.io/blog/national-weather-service-api-omuv)).

**Point forecast.** This is a two-step chain. First call `/points/{lat},{lon}` to resolve the grid cell, then call the forecast URL for that grid, such as `/gridpoints/{office}/{x},{y}/forecast` ([Apify actor](https://apify.com/jungle_synthesizer/nws-weather-alerts-point-forecast-scraper)). The official docs give a gridpoint forecast example at `/gridpoints/TOP/31,80/forecast` ([weather.gov](https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-API)).

**User-Agent.** There's no published hard rate limit, but NWS asks for a polite User-Agent that identifies you ([Apify actor](https://apify.com/jungle_synthesizer/nws-weather-alerts-point-forecast-scraper)). Without one, requests may be rejected, but I didn't find a source confirming the exact failure behavior.

**Coverage and caching.**
- Coverage is US-only. A non-US point returns a 404 with the title "Data Unavailable For Requested Point" ([Browserless skill](https://cloud.browserless.io/skills/weather.gov/get-forecast)).
- A third-party skill reports caching of 24 hours on `/points/` and 2 minutes on `/forecast` ([Browserless skill](https://cloud.browserless.io/skills/weather.gov/get-forecast)). I'd check this against the official spec before relying on it.
- The `/alerts` endpoint covers alerts issued in the past seven days ([weather.gov](https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-API)).

# Spec v1-hubs-and-data — HubRisk

## Context

v0 shipped the platform. v1 gives it data: a hub registry, ten years of daily weather history per hub from the
Open-Meteo archive committed as Parquet and queried with DuckDB, and a NOAA NWS client for live alerts and the
7-day forecast. No scoring, no tools, no prompts yet (v2, v3); v1 only makes `ToolContext` carry the handles
those specs will use and lets `/health` report data coverage.

**Size:** ~600 lines of code in a new `app/data` package, ~250 lines of tests, one real ingest run (15 HTTP
requests, ~55k rows, well under 1 MB of Parquet committed). One commit series. New dependency: `duckdb`.

## Shaping answers (from HANDOFF.md and the product docs; no open questions)

- **What:** roadmap item 2. Hubs as data, history snapshot, live client, offline fakes for all of it.
- **Visuals:** none.
- **References:** v0 patterns to reuse: `app/config.py` loaders (`load_agent_config` style, versioned YAML),
  `app/llm/models.py::retrying_http_client` (httpx2 + tenacity transport, takes `wrapped=` for `MockTransport`),
  `tests/fakes.py` + `conftest.py` fixture style, `cli.compose` as the only composition root,
  `app/api/app.py::Health`.
- **Product alignment:** mission "regions are data, not guesses", "now vs history"; tech-stack "DuckDB over Parquet
  snapshots committed to the repo".
- **Standards applied:** data-sources (primary), python-style, secrets-and-config, testing. Not applied: ai-calls,
  guardrails, budget, evals, deployment (nothing changes there), scoring (v2).

## Decisions

- **Hub registry** `config/hubs.yaml` (versioned): 15 hubs, each `id, name, state, region, lat, lon, county_fips,
  timezone`. Regions are the four US Census regions: Midwest (Chicago, Minneapolis, Detroit, Columbus, Kansas
  City), South (Dallas, Houston, Miami, Atlanta, Memphis), West (Denver, Phoenix, Los Angeles, Seattle),
  Northeast (Newark). `county_fips` is kept for the optional FEMA NRI signal.
- **History source:** Open-Meteo archive `GET https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive` with
  `daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,snowfall_sum,wind_gusts_10m_max`, hub timezone,
  2016-01-01..2025-12-31, one request per hub. Units are metric defaults (°C, mm, cm, km/h); the client checks the
  response's `daily_units` against the expected set and fails loudly on a mismatch rather than trusting docs.
- **Snapshot:** `data/snapshots/daily.parquet` (columns `hub_id, date, tmax_c, tmin_c, precip_mm, snow_cm,
  gust_kmh`) plus `data/snapshots/manifest.json` (source, fetched_at, start, end, hubs_version, hub count, row
  count). Written and read with DuckDB only (no pandas/pyarrow): rows go into a temp table via `executemany`, then
  `COPY ... TO (FORMAT PARQUET)`; reading is `read_parquet`.
- **Store:** `Store(snapshot_dir)` owns one in-process DuckDB connection with a `daily` view over the Parquet.
  v1 methods: `daily(hub_id, start, end)`, `coverage()` per hub, `years(hub_id)` (complete years only, ≥ 360 rows),
  `manifest`. v2 adds the threshold queries.
- **Live source:** `NWSClient(http, user_agent, cache_ttl_s=600, now)`; `alerts(hub)` via
  `/alerts/active?point=lat,lon`, `forecast(hub)` via `/points/{lat},{lon}` then the returned forecast URL.
  Every request carries `User-Agent` (NWS requires it; value from `NWS_USER_AGENT`, default names the repo).
  Results cached per hub and kind for the TTL. Any failure returns `Live(available=False, reason=...)`; the
  client never raises into a caller.
- **HTTP:** both clients take an `httpx2.AsyncClient`; production builds it with `retrying_http_client` (429/5xx/
  network retries); tests pass `MockTransport` with recorded JSON fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`.
- **Ingest:** `agent ingest [--start] [--end] [--hub ID]... [--out DIR]`, sequential requests with a short pause,
  replaces the snapshot atomically (write to temp, rename). Run once locally; the result is committed.
- **Wiring:** `ToolContext` gains `hubs: HubRegistry`, `store: Store | None`, `nws: NWSClient | None` (None in
  unit tests that don't need them). `compose` builds them; a missing snapshot logs a warning and leaves `store`
  None, the app still serves. `Health` gains `data: {hubs, start, end, rows} | None`.
- **Settings:** `NWS_USER_AGENT`, `SNAPSHOT_DIR` (default `data/snapshots`).
- `.gitignore` already keeps `data/snapshots/` committable (v0).

## Spec folder

`C:\ai-projects\hubrisk\agent-os\specs\2026-10-28-v1-hubs-and-data\`: `spec.md` (canonical), `shape.md`,
`standards.md` (data-sources, python-style, secrets-and-config, testing), `references.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (each → `test_criterion_<n>_<slug>` in `tests/test_v1_hubs_and_data.py`)

1. `config/hubs.yaml` validates: a version string, at least 12 hubs with unique ids, lat/lon in range, 5-digit county FIPS, region in {Midwest, South, West, Northeast} with at least three Midwest hubs, and an IANA timezone.
2. `HubRegistry.find` resolves an id or display name case-insensitively ("miami", "Kansas City") and returns None for an unknown hub; `in_region("midwest")` filters case-insensitively; `regions()` lists the regions present.
3. The Open-Meteo client requests the five daily variables with the hub's timezone and date range, parses a recorded response into `DailyRow`s, and raises `SourceError` when `daily_units` differ from the expected units.
4. The Open-Meteo client keeps a day whose values are null (fields None) and raises `SourceError` after the transport's retries on an HTTP error.
5. `write_snapshot` writes `daily.parquet` and `manifest.json`; `Store` reads them back and a synthetic row set round-trips unchanged, ordered by hub and date.
6. `Store.daily` returns rows in a date range in order, `Store.coverage` gives first date, last date and row count per hub, and `Store.years` lists only complete years.
7. `ingest` fetches every hub (or the `--hub` subset) through the client, writes one snapshot, and a re-run replaces it; `agent ingest` is a CLI command.
8. The NWS client resolves `/points` then the forecast URL into `ForecastPeriod`s, parses active alerts into `Alert`s, and sends the configured User-Agent on every request.
9. NWS results are cached per hub for `cache_ttl_s` (a second call within the TTL makes no request); a failed request returns `available=False` with a reason and does not raise.
10. `compose` builds `ToolContext` with the registry, store and NWS client; with no snapshot present the store is None, a warning is logged, and the app still composes and answers in test mode.
11. `GET /health` reports `data` with hub count, first and last date and row count when a snapshot is loaded, and `null` when it is missing.
12. The committed snapshot covers every hub in `hubs.yaml` from 2016-01-01 to 2025-12-31 with at least 3,600 rows per hub and no duplicate (hub, date); the manifest's `hubs_version` matches `hubs.yaml`.

## Design (goes into spec.md)

New package `src/app/data/`:
- `hubs.py`: `Hub` (Pydantic, validators for FIPS/region/timezone), `HubRegistry` (`load(path)`, `all`, `by_id`,
  `find`, `in_region`, `regions`, `version`).
- `openmeteo.py`: `DailyRow` model, `EXPECTED_UNITS`, `SourceError`, `OpenMeteoClient(http).fetch_daily(hub,
  start, end) -> list[DailyRow]`.
- `snapshot.py`: `Manifest` model, `write_snapshot(rows, manifest, out_dir)`, `SNAPSHOT_FILE`, `MANIFEST_FILE`.
- `store.py`: `Store(snapshot_dir)`, `Coverage` model, `Store.open_if_present(dir) -> Store | None`.
- `nws.py`: `Alert`, `ForecastPeriod`, `Live[T](available, items, fetched_at, reason)`, `NWSClient`.
- `ingest.py`: `async ingest(registry, client, start, end, out_dir, hub_ids=None, pause_s=0.5) -> Manifest`.

Changes: `app/config.py` (`Settings.nws_user_agent`, `Settings.snapshot_dir`), `app/agent/tools.py`
(`ToolContext` fields), `app/cli.py` (`ingest` command; `compose` wiring; health data), `app/api/app.py`
(`Health.data`), `pyproject.toml` (`duckdb>=1.1`), `.env.example`, `docs/DESIGN.md` (data layer section),
`README.md` (data section: what is committed, how to refresh), roadmap closeout.

Fixtures (`tests/fixtures/`): `openmeteo_sample.json` (real response shape, a few days), `nws_points.json`,
`nws_forecast.json`, `nws_alerts.json`. Synthetic Parquet is built in tests through `write_snapshot`.

## Tasks (spec.md order)

1. Save spec documentation.
2. Add `duckdb`, Settings fields, `config/hubs.yaml`, `app/data/hubs.py`.
3. `openmeteo.py`, `snapshot.py`, `store.py` with fixtures and tests.
4. `nws.py` with fixtures and tests.
5. `ingest.py`, `agent ingest`, `compose` wiring, `Health.data`.
6. Run the real ingest once (`uv run agent ingest`), inspect coverage, commit `data/snapshots/`.
7. README and DESIGN updates, roadmap closeout, `ruff`, `pytest`, commit `feat: v1 hubs and data`.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest -q`: v0's 77 plus 12 criterion tests plus unit tests green; coverage test passes.
- `uv run ruff check src tests` clean.
- `uv run agent ingest` completes; `manifest.json` shows 15 hubs, 2016-01-01..2025-12-31, ~54,800 rows.
- `uv run agent serve --test` then `GET /health` shows `data` with 15 hubs and the date range.
- Prompts and models unchanged, so no new eval report is required.

page, sessions, rate limits, eval runner, offline tests, CI, Render Blueprint. A working scaffold of exactly this
(50 test functions, 55 collected, all green) exists in `C:\ai-projects\agent-assignment`; the roadmap says lift it
under its own spec. This plan shapes that spec and the lift.

**Size:** ~1,900 lines lifted as-is, ~20 small edits (renames, two fixes), one new test file (~18 criterion tests),
a per-spec change to the coverage test, README + DESIGN.md skeletons. One commit series, roughly 2 hours.

## Shaping answers (from HANDOFF.md, no open questions)

# Spec v1-hubs-and-data — HubRisk

## Context

v0 shipped the platform. v1 gives it data: a hub registry, ten years of daily weather history per hub from the
Open-Meteo archive committed as Parquet and queried with DuckDB, and a NOAA NWS client for live alerts and the
7-day forecast. No scoring, no tools, no prompts yet (v2, v3); v1 only makes `ToolContext` carry the handles
those specs will use and lets `/health` report data coverage.

**Size:** ~600 lines of code in a new `app/data` package, ~250 lines of tests, one real ingest run (15 HTTP
requests, ~55k rows, well under 1 MB of Parquet committed). One commit series. New dependency: `duckdb`.

## Shaping answers (from HANDOFF.md and the product docs; no open questions)

- **What:** roadmap item 2. Hubs as data, history snapshot, live client, offline fakes for all of it.
- **Visuals:** none.
- **References:** v0 patterns to reuse: `app/config.py` loaders (`load_agent_config` style, versioned YAML),
  `app/llm/models.py::retrying_http_client` (httpx2 + tenacity transport, takes `wrapped=` for `MockTransport`),
  `tests/fakes.py` + `conftest.py` fixture style, `cli.compose` as the only composition root,
  `app/api/app.py::Health`.
- **Product alignment:** mission "regions are data, not guesses", "now vs history"; tech-stack "DuckDB over Parquet
  snapshots committed to the repo".
- **Standards applied:** data-sources (primary), python-style, secrets-and-config, testing. Not applied: ai-calls,
  guardrails, budget, evals, deployment (nothing changes there), scoring (v2).

## Decisions

- **Hub registry** `config/hubs.yaml` (versioned): 15 hubs, each `id, name, state, region, lat, lon, county_fips,
  timezone`. Regions are the four US Census regions: Midwest (Chicago, Minneapolis, Detroit, Columbus, Kansas
  City), South (Dallas, Houston, Miami, Atlanta, Memphis), West (Denver, Phoenix, Los Angeles, Seattle),
  Northeast (Newark). `county_fips` is kept for the optional FEMA NRI signal.
- **History source:** Open-Meteo archive `GET https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive` with
  `daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,snowfall_sum,wind_gusts_10m_max`, hub timezone,
  2016-01-01..2025-12-31, one request per hub. Units are metric defaults (°C, mm, cm, km/h); the client checks the
  response's `daily_units` against the expected set and fails loudly on a mismatch rather than trusting docs.
- **Snapshot:** `data/snapshots/daily.parquet` (columns `hub_id, date, tmax_c, tmin_c, precip_mm, snow_cm,
  gust_kmh`) plus `data/snapshots/manifest.json` (source, fetched_at, start, end, hubs_version, hub count, row
  count). Written and read with DuckDB only (no pandas/pyarrow): rows go into a temp table via `executemany`, then
  `COPY ... TO (FORMAT PARQUET)`; reading is `read_parquet`.
- **Store:** `Store(snapshot_dir)` owns one in-process DuckDB connection with a `daily` view over the Parquet.
  v1 methods: `daily(hub_id, start, end)`, `coverage()` per hub, `years(hub_id)` (complete years only, ≥ 360 rows),
  `manifest`. v2 adds the threshold queries.
- **Live source:** `NWSClient(http, user_agent, cache_ttl_s=600, now)`; `alerts(hub)` via
  `/alerts/active?point=lat,lon`, `forecast(hub)` via `/points/{lat},{lon}` then the returned forecast URL.
  Every request carries `User-Agent` (NWS requires it; value from `NWS_USER_AGENT`, default names the repo).
  Results cached per hub and kind for the TTL. Any failure returns `Live(available=False, reason=...)`; the
  client never raises into a caller.
- **HTTP:** both clients take an `httpx2.AsyncClient`; production builds it with `retrying_http_client` (429/5xx/
  network retries); tests pass `MockTransport` with recorded JSON fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`.
- **Ingest:** `agent ingest [--start] [--end] [--hub ID]... [--out DIR]`, sequential requests with a short pause,
  replaces the snapshot atomically (write to temp, rename). Run once locally; the result is committed.
- **Wiring:** `ToolContext` gains `hubs: HubRegistry`, `store: Store | None`, `nws: NWSClient | None` (None in
  unit tests that don't need them). `compose` builds them; a missing snapshot logs a warning and leaves `store`
  None, the app still serves. `Health` gains `data: {hubs, start, end, rows} | None`.
- **Settings:** `NWS_USER_AGENT`, `SNAPSHOT_DIR` (default `data/snapshots`).
- `.gitignore` already keeps `data/snapshots/` committable (v0).

## Spec folder

`C:\ai-projects\hubrisk\agent-os\specs\2026-10-28-v1-hubs-and-data\`: `spec.md` (canonical), `shape.md`,
`standards.md` (data-sources, python-style, secrets-and-config, testing), `references.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (each → `test_criterion_<n>_<slug>` in `tests/test_v1_hubs_and_data.py`)

1. `config/hubs.yaml` validates: a version string, at least 12 hubs with unique ids, lat/lon in range, 5-digit county FIPS, region in {Midwest, South, West, Northeast} with at least three Midwest hubs, and an IANA timezone.
2. `HubRegistry.find` resolves an id or display name case-insensitively ("miami", "Kansas City") and returns None for an unknown hub; `in_region("midwest")` filters case-insensitively; `regions()` lists the regions present.
3. The Open-Meteo client requests the five daily variables with the hub's timezone and date range, parses a recorded response into `DailyRow`s, and raises `SourceError` when `daily_units` differ from the expected units.
4. The Open-Meteo client keeps a day whose values are null (fields None) and raises `SourceError` after the transport's retries on an HTTP error.
5. `write_snapshot` writes `daily.parquet` and `manifest.json`; `Store` reads them back and a synthetic row set round-trips unchanged, ordered by hub and date.
6. `Store.daily` returns rows in a date range in order, `Store.coverage` gives first date, last date and row count per hub, and `Store.years` lists only complete years.
7. `ingest` fetches every hub (or the `--hub` subset) through the client, writes one snapshot, and a re-run replaces it; `agent ingest` is a CLI command.
8. The NWS client resolves `/points` then the forecast URL into `ForecastPeriod`s, parses active alerts into `Alert`s, and sends the configured User-Agent on every request.
9. NWS results are cached per hub for `cache_ttl_s` (a second call within the TTL makes no request); a failed request returns `available=False` with a reason and does not raise.
10. `compose` builds `ToolContext` with the registry, store and NWS client; with no snapshot present the store is None, a warning is logged, and the app still composes and answers in test mode.
11. `GET /health` reports `data` with hub count, first and last date and row count when a snapshot is loaded, and `null` when it is missing.
12. The committed snapshot covers every hub in `hubs.yaml` from 2016-01-01 to 2025-12-31 with at least 3,600 rows per hub and no duplicate (hub, date); the manifest's `hubs_version` matches `hubs.yaml`.

## Design (goes into spec.md)

New package `src/app/data/`:
- `hubs.py`: `Hub` (Pydantic, validators for FIPS/region/timezone), `HubRegistry` (`load(path)`, `all`, `by_id`,
  `find`, `in_region`, `regions`, `version`).
- `openmeteo.py`: `DailyRow` model, `EXPECTED_UNITS`, `SourceError`, `OpenMeteoClient(http).fetch_daily(hub,
  start, end) -> list[DailyRow]`.
- `snapshot.py`: `Manifest` model, `write_snapshot(rows, manifest, out_dir)`, `SNAPSHOT_FILE`, `MANIFEST_FILE`.
- `store.py`: `Store(snapshot_dir)`, `Coverage` model, `Store.open_if_present(dir) -> Store | None`.
- `nws.py`: `Alert`, `ForecastPeriod`, `Live[T](available, items, fetched_at, reason)`, `NWSClient`.
- `ingest.py`: `async ingest(registry, client, start, end, out_dir, hub_ids=None, pause_s=0.5) -> Manifest`.

Changes: `app/config.py` (`Settings.nws_user_agent`, `Settings.snapshot_dir`), `app/agent/tools.py`
(`ToolContext` fields), `app/cli.py` (`ingest` command; `compose` wiring; health data), `app/api/app.py`
(`Health.data`), `pyproject.toml` (`duckdb>=1.1`), `.env.example`, `docs/DESIGN.md` (data layer section),
`README.md` (data section: what is committed, how to refresh), roadmap closeout.

Fixtures (`tests/fixtures/`): `openmeteo_sample.json` (real response shape, a few days), `nws_points.json`,
`nws_forecast.json`, `nws_alerts.json`. Synthetic Parquet is built in tests through `write_snapshot`.

## Tasks (spec.md order)

1. Save spec documentation.
2. Add `duckdb`, Settings fields, `config/hubs.yaml`, `app/data/hubs.py`.
3. `openmeteo.py`, `snapshot.py`, `store.py` with fixtures and tests.
4. `nws.py` with fixtures and tests.
5. `ingest.py`, `agent ingest`, `compose` wiring, `Health.data`.
6. Run the real ingest once (`uv run agent ingest`), inspect coverage, commit `data/snapshots/`.
7. README and DESIGN updates, roadmap closeout, `ruff`, `pytest`, commit `feat: v1 hubs and data`.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest -q`: v0's 77 plus 12 criterion tests plus unit tests green; coverage test passes.
- `uv run ruff check src tests` clean.
- `uv run agent ingest` completes; `manifest.json` shows 15 hubs, 2016-01-01..2025-12-31, ~54,800 rows.

3. The Open-Meteo client requests the five daily variables with the hub's timezone and date range, parses a recorded response into `DailyRow`s, and raises `SourceError` when `daily_units` differ from the expected units.
4. The Open-Meteo client keeps a day whose values are null (fields None) and raises `SourceError` after the transport's retries on an HTTP error.
5. `write_snapshot` writes `daily.parquet` and `manifest.json`; `Store` reads them back and a synthetic row set round-trips unchanged, ordered by hub and date.
6. `Store.daily` returns rows in a date range in order, `Store.coverage` gives first date, last date and row count per hub, and `Store.years` lists only complete years.
7. `ingest` fetches every hub (or the `--hub` subset) through the client, writes one snapshot, and a re-run replaces it; `agent ingest` is a CLI command.
8. The NWS client resolves `/points` then the forecast URL into `ForecastPeriod`s, parses active alerts into `Alert`s, and sends the configured User-Agent on every request.
9. NWS results are cached per hub for `cache_ttl_s` (a second call within the TTL makes no request); a failed request returns `available=False` with a reason and does not raise.
10. `compose` builds `ToolContext` with the registry, store and NWS client; with no snapshot present the store is None, a warning is logged, and the app still composes and answers in test mode.
11. `GET /health` reports `data` with hub count, first and last date and row count when a snapshot is loaded, and `null` when it is missing.
12. The committed snapshot covers every hub in `hubs.yaml` from 2016-01-01 to 2025-12-31 with at least 3,600 rows per hub and no duplicate (hub, date); the manifest's `hubs_version` matches `hubs.yaml`.

New package `src/app/data/`:

- `hubs.py`: `Hub` (id, name, state, region, lat, lon, county_fips, timezone; validators for FIPS, region and
  timezone) and `HubRegistry` (`load(path)`, `all`, `by_id`, `find`, `in_region`, `regions`, `version`). Regions
  are the four US Census regions, so "Midwest hubs" is a filter over data.
- `openmeteo.py`: `DailyRow(hub_id, date, tmax_c, tmin_c, precip_mm, snow_cm, gust_kmh)`, `EXPECTED_UNITS`,
  `SourceError`, `OpenMeteoClient(http).fetch_daily(hub, start, end)`. One request per hub:
  `daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,snowfall_sum,wind_gusts_10m_max`, the hub's
  timezone. The response's `daily_units` are checked against the expected metric units (°C, mm, cm, km/h).
- `snapshot.py`: `Manifest(source, fetched_at, start, end, hubs_version, hubs, rows)`, `write_snapshot(rows,
  manifest, out_dir)` using DuckDB only (temp table → `COPY TO ... (FORMAT PARQUET)`), atomic replace.
- `store.py`: `Store(snapshot_dir)` with one in-process DuckDB connection and a `daily` view over the Parquet;
  `daily(hub_id, start, end)`, `coverage()`, `years(hub_id)` (complete years, ≥ 360 rows), `manifest`;
  `Store.open_if_present(dir)`.
- `nws.py`: `Alert`, `ForecastPeriod`, `Live(available, items, fetched_at, reason)`, `NWSClient(http, user_agent,
  cache_ttl_s, now)` with `alerts(hub)` (`/alerts/active?point=`) and `forecast(hub)` (`/points` then the
  forecast URL). Per-hub cache; failures degrade to `available=False`.
- `ingest.py`: `ingest(registry, client, start, end, out_dir, hub_ids, pause_s)`; `agent ingest` wraps it.

committing Parquet means deploys need no network and the demo cannot be broken by an upstream outage.

6. Run the real ingest once, inspect coverage, commit `data/snapshots/`.

# v1 hubs and data — Shaping Notes

## Scope

Hub registry, Open-Meteo daily history 2016–2025 as committed Parquet queried by DuckDB, NOAA NWS live client,
`agent ingest`, `ToolContext` handles and `/health` coverage. No scoring, tools or prompts.

## Decisions

- 15 hubs in the four US Census regions; `county_fips` kept for an optional FEMA NRI signal.
- Open-Meteo archive, five daily variables, one request per hub; units verified from the response's
  `daily_units`, not assumed from docs.
- Snapshot written and read with DuckDB only (no pandas/pyarrow); atomic replace; manifest records provenance.
- NWS requires a User-Agent; it comes from `NWS_USER_AGENT` with a default naming the repo. Results cached per
  hub for ten minutes; failures degrade to `available=False` and never raise into the agent.
- Both clients take an `httpx2.AsyncClient` so tests inject `MockTransport` with recorded fixtures.
- A missing snapshot is a warning, not a crash: the app serves, `/health` says `data: null`.
- `Store.years` counts a year complete at ≥ 360 rows so a few missing days do not drop a year.

## Context

- **Visuals:** none.
- **References:** v0 `app/config.py` loaders, `app/llm/models.py::retrying_http_client`, `tests/fakes.py`,
  `cli.compose`, `app/api/app.py::Health`.
- **Product alignment:** mission "regions are data, not guesses" and "now vs history"; tech-stack storage choice.

## Standards Applied

- data-sources — the subject of this spec.
- python-style — new `data` package, Pydantic at every boundary, typed errors.
- secrets-and-config — `NWS_USER_AGENT`, `SNAPSHOT_DIR`; versioned `hubs.yaml`.
- testing — MockTransport fixtures, synthetic Parquet, criterion tests in `tests/test_v1_hubs_and_data.py`.

"""Parquet snapshot of the daily history plus a manifest with provenance. DuckDB writes it; no pandas or pyarrow."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from datetime import date, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb
from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.data.openmeteo import DailyRow

SNAPSHOT_FILE = "daily.parquet"
MANIFEST_FILE = "manifest.json"
SCHEMA = "hub_id VARCHAR, date DATE, tmax_c DOUBLE, tmin_c DOUBLE, precip_mm DOUBLE, snow_cm DOUBLE, gust_kmh DOUBLE"


class Manifest(BaseModel):
    source: str
    fetched_at: datetime
    start: date
    end: date
    hubs_version: str
    hubs: int
    rows: int


def write_snapshot(rows: list[DailyRow], manifest: Manifest, out_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Write daily.parquet and manifest.json, replacing any previous snapshot atomically."""
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE daily ({SCHEMA})")
    if rows:
        con.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO daily VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            [(r.hub_id, r.date, r.tmax_c, r.tmin_c, r.precip_mm, r.snow_cm, r.gust_kmh) for r in rows],
        )
    tmp = out_dir / (SNAPSHOT_FILE + ".tmp")
    con.execute(f"COPY (SELECT * FROM daily ORDER BY hub_id, date) TO '{tmp.as_posix()}' (FORMAT PARQUET)")
    con.close()
    os.replace(tmp, out_dir / SNAPSHOT_FILE)
    (out_dir / MANIFEST_FILE).write_text(manifest.model_dump_json(indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

"""NOAA NWS client: active alerts and the 7-day forecast per hub. Keyless, needs a User-Agent, cached per hub.

A failed call degrades to `available=False` with a reason; the agent reports it in `limitations` instead of crashing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar

import httpx2
from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.data.hubs import Hub

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
NWS_URL = "https://api.weather.gov"
T = TypeVar("T")


class Alert(BaseModel):
    event: str
    severity: str | None = None
    urgency: str | None = None
    headline: str | None = None
    onset: datetime | None = None
    ends: datetime | None = None
    area: str | None = None


class ForecastPeriod(BaseModel):
    name: str
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    is_daytime: bool = True
    temperature: int | None = None
    temperature_unit: str | None = None
    wind_speed: str | None = None
    wind_direction: str | None = None
    precipitation_chance: int | None = None
    short_forecast: str = ""


class Live(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    available: bool = True
    items: list[T] = []
    fetched_at: datetime | None = None
    reason: str | None = None


class NWSClient:
    def __init__(
        self, http: httpx2.AsyncClient, user_agent: str, *, base_url: str = NWS_URL, cache_ttl_s: float = 600.0,
        failure_ttl_s: float = 60.0, now: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
    ) -> None:
        self.http, self.user_agent, self.base_url = http, user_agent, base_url
        self.cache_ttl_s, self.failure_ttl_s, self._now = cache_ttl_s, failure_ttl_s, now
        self._cache: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, Live[Any]]] = {}

    async def alerts(self, hub: Hub) -> Live[Alert]:
        return await self._cached("alerts", hub, self._fetch_alerts)

    async def forecast(self, hub: Hub) -> Live[ForecastPeriod]:
        return await self._cached("forecast", hub, self._fetch_forecast)

    async def _cached(self, kind: str, hub: Hub, fetch: Callable[[Hub], Awaitable[Live[Any]]]) -> Live[Any]:
        key = (kind, hub.id)
        if hit := self._cache.get(key):
            stored_at, live = hit
            ttl = self.cache_ttl_s if live.available else self.failure_ttl_s
            if self._now() - stored_at < ttl:
                return live
        try:
            live = await fetch(hub)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - any failure of a live source degrades, never crashes a turn
            log.warning("nws %s for %s unavailable: %r", kind, hub.id, e)
            live = Live(available=False, reason=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200])
        self._cache[key] = (self._now(), live)
        return live

    async def _get(self, url: str, params: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        headers = {"User-Agent": self.user_agent, "Accept": "application/geo+json"}
        r = await self.http.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()

    @staticmethod
    def _point(hub: Hub) -> str:
        return f"{hub.lat:.4f},{hub.lon:.4f}"

    async def _fetch_alerts(self, hub: Hub) -> Live[Alert]:
        data = await self._get(f"{self.base_url}/alerts/active", params={"point": self._point(hub)})
        items = []
        for feature in data.get("features") or []:
            p = feature.get("properties") or {}
            items.append(Alert(
                event=p.get("event") or "", severity=p.get("severity"), urgency=p.get("urgency"),
                headline=p.get("headline"), onset=p.get("onset"), ends=p.get("ends"), area=p.get("areaDesc"),
            ))
        return Live(items=items, fetched_at=datetime.now(UTC))

    async def _fetch_forecast(self, hub: Hub) -> Live[ForecastPeriod]:
        points = await self._get(f"{self.base_url}/points/{self._point(hub)}")
        data = await self._get(points["properties"]["forecast"])
        items = [
            ForecastPeriod(
                name=p["name"], start=p["startTime"], end=p["endTime"], is_daytime=p.get("isDaytime", True),
                temperature=p.get("temperature"), temperature_unit=p.get("temperatureUnit"),
                wind_speed=p.get("windSpeed"), wind_direction=p.get("windDirection"),
                precipitation_chance=(p.get("probabilityOfPrecipitation") or {}).get("value"),
                short_forecast=p.get("shortForecast") or "",
            )
            for p in data["properties"]["periods"]
        ]
        return Live(items=items, fetched_at=datetime.now(UTC))

"""Parquet snapshot of the daily history plus a manifest with provenance. DuckDB writes it; no pandas or pyarrow."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from datetime import date, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb
from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.data.openmeteo import DailyRow

SNAPSHOT_FILE = "daily.parquet"
MANIFEST_FILE = "manifest.json"
SCHEMA = "hub_id VARCHAR, date DATE, tmax_c DOUBLE, tmin_c DOUBLE, precip_mm DOUBLE, snow_cm DOUBLE, gust_kmh DOUBLE"


class Manifest(BaseModel):
    source: str
    fetched_at: datetime
    start: date
    end: date
    hubs_version: str
    hubs: int
    rows: int


def write_snapshot(rows: list[DailyRow], manifest: Manifest, out_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Write daily.parquet and manifest.json, replacing any previous snapshot atomically."""
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE daily ({SCHEMA})")
    if rows:
        con.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO daily VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            [(r.hub_id, r.date, r.tmax_c, r.tmin_c, r.precip_mm, r.snow_cm, r.gust_kmh) for r in rows],
        )
    tmp = out_dir / (SNAPSHOT_FILE + ".tmp")
    con.execute(f"COPY (SELECT * FROM daily ORDER BY hub_id, date) TO '{tmp.as_posix()}' (FORMAT PARQUET)")
    con.close()
    os.replace(tmp, out_dir / SNAPSHOT_FILE)
    (out_dir / MANIFEST_FILE).write_text(manifest.model_dump_json(indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

"""NOAA NWS client: active alerts and the 7-day forecast per hub. Keyless, needs a User-Agent, cached per hub.

A failed call degrades to `available=False` with a reason; the agent reports it in `limitations` instead of crashing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar

import httpx2
from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.data.hubs import Hub

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
NWS_URL = "https://api.weather.gov"
T = TypeVar("T")


class Alert(BaseModel):
    event: str
    severity: str | None = None
    urgency: str | None = None
    headline: str | None = None
    onset: datetime | None = None
    ends: datetime | None = None
    area: str | None = None


class ForecastPeriod(BaseModel):
    name: str
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    is_daytime: bool = True
    temperature: int | None = None
    temperature_unit: str | None = None
    wind_speed: str | None = None
    wind_direction: str | None = None
    precipitation_chance: int | None = None
    short_forecast: str = ""


class Live(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    available: bool = True
    items: list[T] = []
    fetched_at: datetime | None = None
    reason: str | None = None


class NWSClient:
    def __init__(
        self, http: httpx2.AsyncClient, user_agent: str, *, base_url: str = NWS_URL, cache_ttl_s: float = 600.0,
        failure_ttl_s: float = 60.0, now: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
    ) -> None:
        self.http, self.user_agent, self.base_url = http, user_agent, base_url
        self.cache_ttl_s, self.failure_ttl_s, self._now = cache_ttl_s, failure_ttl_s, now
        self._cache: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, Live[Any]]] = {}

    async def alerts(self, hub: Hub) -> Live[Alert]:
        return await self._cached("alerts", hub, self._fetch_alerts)

    async def forecast(self, hub: Hub) -> Live[ForecastPeriod]:
        return await self._cached("forecast", hub, self._fetch_forecast)

    async def _cached(self, kind: str, hub: Hub, fetch: Callable[[Hub], Awaitable[Live[Any]]]) -> Live[Any]:
        key = (kind, hub.id)
        if hit := self._cache.get(key):
            stored_at, live = hit
            ttl = self.cache_ttl_s if live.available else self.failure_ttl_s
            if self._now() - stored_at < ttl:
                return live
        try:
            live = await fetch(hub)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - any failure of a live source degrades, never crashes a turn
            log.warning("nws %s for %s unavailable: %r", kind, hub.id, e)
            live = Live(available=False, reason=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200])
        self._cache[key] = (self._now(), live)
        return live

    async def _get(self, url: str, params: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        headers = {"User-Agent": self.user_agent, "Accept": "application/geo+json"}
        r = await self.http.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()

    @staticmethod
    def _point(hub: Hub) -> str:
        return f"{hub.lat:.4f},{hub.lon:.4f}"

    async def _fetch_alerts(self, hub: Hub) -> Live[Alert]:
        data = await self._get(f"{self.base_url}/alerts/active", params={"point": self._point(hub)})
        items = []
        for feature in data.get("features") or []:
            p = feature.get("properties") or {}
            items.append(Alert(
                event=p.get("event") or "", severity=p.get("severity"), urgency=p.get("urgency"),
                headline=p.get("headline"), onset=p.get("onset"), ends=p.get("ends"), area=p.get("areaDesc"),
            ))
        return Live(items=items, fetched_at=datetime.now(UTC))

    async def _fetch_forecast(self, hub: Hub) -> Live[ForecastPeriod]:
        points = await self._get(f"{self.base_url}/points/{self._point(hub)}")
        data = await self._get(points["properties"]["forecast"])
        items = [
            ForecastPeriod(
                name=p["name"], start=p["startTime"], end=p["endTime"], is_daytime=p.get("isDaytime", True),
                temperature=p.get("temperature"), temperature_unit=p.get("temperatureUnit"),
                wind_speed=p.get("windSpeed"), wind_direction=p.get("windDirection"),
                precipitation_chance=(p.get("probabilityOfPrecipitation") or {}).get("value"),
                short_forecast=p.get("shortForecast") or "",
            )
            for p in data["properties"]["periods"]
        ]
        return Live(items=items, fetched_at=datetime.now(UTC))

"""Acceptance criteria of agent-os/specs/2026-10-28-v1-hubs-and-data, one test per criterion, all offline."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import httpx2
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import ValidationError
from typer.testing import CliRunner

from app import cli as cli_module
from app.agent.core import Conversation
from app.api.app import create_app
from app.api.sessions import SessionStore
from app.config import ROOT
from app.data.hubs import Hub, HubRegistry
from app.data.ingest import ingest
from app.data.nws import NWSClient
from app.data.openmeteo import DailyRow, OpenMeteoClient, SourceError
from app.data.snapshot import MANIFEST_FILE, SNAPSHOT_FILE, Manifest, write_snapshot
from app.data.store import DataSummary, Store
from app.llm.models import retrying_http_client

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures"
DENVER = Hub(
    id="denver", name="Denver", state="CO", region="West", lat=39.7392, lon=-104.9903, county_fips="08031",
    timezone="America/Denver",
)


def fixture(name: str) -> dict:
    return json.loads((FIXTURES / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def manifest(rows: list[DailyRow], hubs: int = 1, version: str = "1.0.0") -> Manifest:
    return Manifest(
        source="test", fetched_at=datetime.now(UTC), start=min(r.date for r in rows), end=max(r.date for r in rows),
        hubs_version=version, hubs=hubs, rows=len(rows),
    )


def synthetic(hub_id: str, start: date, days: int) -> list[DailyRow]:
    return [
        DailyRow(hub_id=hub_id, date=start + timedelta(days=i), tmax_c=10 + i % 7, tmin_c=-1.0, precip_mm=i % 3,
                 snow_cm=0.5 if i % 10 == 0 else 0.0, gust_kmh=30 + i % 20)
        for i in range(days)
    ]


def client_for(handler) -> httpx2.AsyncClient:
    return httpx2.AsyncClient(transport=httpx2.MockTransport(handler))


def test_criterion_1_hubs_yaml_validates():
    reg = HubRegistry.load()
    assert reg.version and len(reg.all) >= 12 and len({h.id for h in reg.all}) == len(reg.all)
    assert len(reg.in_region("Midwest")) >= 3
    base = DENVER.model_dump()
    for bad in ({"county_fips": "8031"}, {"region": "Mountain"}, {"timezone": "Mars/Olympus"}, {"lat": 95}):
        with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
            Hub(**{**base, **bad})


def test_criterion_2_registry_lookup_is_case_insensitive():
    reg = HubRegistry.load()
    assert reg.find("miami").id == "miami" and reg.find("Kansas City").id == "kansas-city"
    assert reg.find("KANSAS-CITY").id == "kansas-city" and reg.find("atlantis") is None
    assert {h.id for h in reg.in_region("midwest")} == {"chicago", "minneapolis", "detroit", "columbus", "kansas-city"}
    assert reg.regions() == ["Midwest", "Northeast", "South", "West"]


async def test_criterion_3_openmeteo_request_parse_and_unit_check():
    seen: list[httpx2.Request] = []

    def handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
        seen.append(request)
        return httpx2.Response(200, json=fixture("openmeteo_sample.json"))

    rows = await OpenMeteoClient(client_for(handler)).fetch_daily(DENVER, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 4))
    params = seen[0].url.params
    assert params["timezone"] == "America/Denver" and params["start_date"] == "2024-01-01" and params["end_date"] == "2024-01-04"
    assert params["daily"].split(",") == [
        "temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min", "precipitation_sum", "snowfall_sum", "wind_gusts_10m_max",
    ]
    assert len(rows) == 4 and rows[3] == DailyRow(
        hub_id="denver", date=date(2024, 1, 4), tmax_c=1.5, tmin_c=-6.3, precip_mm=0.1, snow_cm=0.07, gust_kmh=16.2
    )
    wrong = fixture("openmeteo_sample.json")
    wrong["daily_units"]["wind_gusts_10m_max"] = "mp/h"
    with pytest.raises(SourceError, match="units"):
        await OpenMeteoClient(client_for(lambda r: httpx2.Response(200, json=wrong))).fetch_daily(DENVER, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 4))


async def test_criterion_4_openmeteo_nulls_kept_and_http_errors_typed():
    payload = fixture("openmeteo_sample.json")
    payload["daily"]["snowfall_sum"][1] = None
    rows = await OpenMeteoClient(client_for(lambda r: httpx2.Response(200, json=payload))).fetch_daily(DENVER, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 4))
    assert len(rows) == 4 and rows[1].snow_cm is None and rows[1].tmax_c == 6.9
    calls: list[int] = []

    def down(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
        calls.append(1)
        return httpx2.Response(503, json={"error": True})

    http = retrying_http_client(attempts=2, timeout_s=5, max_wait_s=0, wrapped=httpx2.MockTransport(down))
    with pytest.raises(SourceError, match="open-meteo denver"):
        await OpenMeteoClient(http).fetch_daily(DENVER, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 4))
    assert len(calls) == 2


def test_criterion_5_snapshot_round_trip(tmp_path: Path):
    rows = synthetic("b", date(2020, 1, 1), 3) + synthetic("a", date(2020, 1, 1), 3)
    rows[0], rows[1] = rows[1], rows[0]
    m = manifest(rows, hubs=2)
    write_snapshot(rows, m, tmp_path)
    assert (tmp_path / SNAPSHOT_FILE).exists() and (tmp_path / MANIFEST_FILE).exists()
    store = Store(tmp_path)
    assert store.manifest == m
    assert store.daily("a") == sorted((r for r in rows if r.hub_id == "a"), key=lambda r: r.date)
    assert store.daily("b") == sorted((r for r in rows if r.hub_id == "b"), key=lambda r: r.date)


def test_criterion_6_store_queries(tmp_path: Path):
    rows = synthetic("a", date(2020, 1, 1), 366 + 100)
    write_snapshot(rows, manifest(rows), tmp_path)
    store = Store(tmp_path)
    window = store.daily("a", date(2020, 3, 1), date(2020, 3, 10))
    assert [r.date for r in window] == [date(2020, 3, 1) + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(10)]
    cov = store.coverage()
    assert cov[0].hub_id == "a" and cov[0].start == date(2020, 1, 1) and cov[0].end == date(2021, 4, 10) and cov[0].rows == 466
    assert store.years("a") == [2020]
    assert store.summary() == DataSummary(hubs=1, start=date(2020, 1, 1), end=date(2021, 4, 10), rows=466, fetched_at=store.manifest.fetched_at.isoformat())


class FakeOpenMeteo:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[str] = []

    async def fetch_daily(self, hub: Hub, start: date, end: date) -> list[DailyRow]:
        self.calls.append(hub.id)
        return synthetic(hub.id, start, (end - start).days + 1)


async def test_criterion_7_ingest_writes_one_snapshot_and_replaces(tmp_path: Path):
    reg, fake = HubRegistry.load(), FakeOpenMeteo()
    m = await ingest(reg, fake, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 10), tmp_path, hub_ids=["denver", "miami"], pause_s=0)
    assert fake.calls == ["denver", "miami"] and m.hubs == 2 and m.rows == 20 and m.hubs_version == reg.version
    assert {c.hub_id for c in Store(tmp_path).coverage()} == {"denver", "miami"}
    await ingest(reg, fake, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 10), tmp_path, hub_ids=["denver"], pause_s=0)
    assert [c.hub_id for c in Store(tmp_path).coverage()] == ["denver"]
    m = await ingest(reg, fake, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 2), tmp_path, pause_s=0)
    assert m.hubs == len(reg.all)
    assert CliRunner().invoke(cli_module.cli, ["ingest", "--help"]).exit_code == 0


def nws_handler(seen: list[httpx2.Request]):
    def handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
        seen.append(request)
        path = request.url.path
        if path.startswith("/points/"):

def test_criterion_6_store_queries(tmp_path: Path):
    rows = synthetic("a", date(2020, 1, 1), 366 + 100)
    write_snapshot(rows, manifest(rows), tmp_path)
    store = Store(tmp_path)
    window = store.daily("a", date(2020, 3, 1), date(2020, 3, 10))
    assert [r.date for r in window] == [date(2020, 3, 1) + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(10)]
    cov = store.coverage()
    assert cov[0].hub_id == "a" and cov[0].start == date(2020, 1, 1) and cov[0].end == date(2021, 4, 10) and cov[0].rows == 466
    assert store.years("a") == [2020]
    assert store.summary() == DataSummary(hubs=1, start=date(2020, 1, 1), end=date(2021, 4, 10), rows=466, fetched_at=store.manifest.fetched_at.isoformat())


class FakeOpenMeteo:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[str] = []

    async def fetch_daily(self, hub: Hub, start: date, end: date) -> list[DailyRow]:
        self.calls.append(hub.id)
        return synthetic(hub.id, start, (end - start).days + 1)


async def test_criterion_7_ingest_writes_one_snapshot_and_replaces(tmp_path: Path):
    reg, fake = HubRegistry.load(), FakeOpenMeteo()
    m = await ingest(reg, fake, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 10), tmp_path, hub_ids=["denver", "miami"], pause_s=0)
    assert fake.calls == ["denver", "miami"] and m.hubs == 2 and m.rows == 20 and m.hubs_version == reg.version
    assert {c.hub_id for c in Store(tmp_path).coverage()} == {"denver", "miami"}
    await ingest(reg, fake, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 10), tmp_path, hub_ids=["denver"], pause_s=0)
    assert [c.hub_id for c in Store(tmp_path).coverage()] == ["denver"]
    m = await ingest(reg, fake, date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 2), tmp_path, pause_s=0)
    assert m.hubs == len(reg.all)
    assert CliRunner().invoke(cli_module.cli, ["ingest", "--help"]).exit_code == 0


def nws_handler(seen: list[httpx2.Request]):
    def handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
        seen.append(request)
        path = request.url.path
        if path.startswith("/points/"):
            return httpx2.Response(200, json=fixture("nws_points.json"))
        if path.endswith("/forecast"):
            return httpx2.Response(200, json=fixture("nws_forecast.json"))
        if path == "/alerts/active":
            return httpx2.Response(200, json=fixture("nws_alerts.json"))
        return httpx2.Response(404, json={"title": "Not Found"})

    return handler


async def test_criterion_8_nws_forecast_alerts_and_user_agent():
    seen: list[httpx2.Request] = []
    nws = NWSClient(client_for(nws_handler(seen)), "hubrisk-test (test@example.com)")
    forecast = await nws.forecast(DENVER)
    assert forecast.available and len(forecast.items) == 3 and forecast.items[0].name == "Overnight"
    assert forecast.items[0].temperature_unit == "F" and forecast.items[0].precipitation_chance == 0
    assert [r.url.path for r in seen] == ["/points/39.7392,-104.9903", "/gridpoints/BOU/63,62/forecast"]
    alerts = await nws.alerts(DENVER)
    assert alerts.available and alerts.items[0].event == "Winter Storm Warning" and alerts.items[0].severity == "Severe"
    assert seen[-1].url.params["point"] == "39.7392,-104.9903"
    assert all(r.headers["user-agent"] == "hubrisk-test (test@example.com)" for r in seen)


async def test_criterion_9_nws_cache_and_degradation():
    seen: list[httpx2.Request] = []
    clock = [0.0]
    nws = NWSClient(client_for(nws_handler(seen)), "ua", cache_ttl_s=600, now=lambda: clock[0])
    await nws.alerts(DENVER)
    await nws.alerts(DENVER)
    assert len(seen) == 1
    clock[0] = 601.0
    await nws.alerts(DENVER)
    assert len(seen) == 2
    broken = NWSClient(client_for(lambda r: httpx2.Response(503, json={})), "ua")
    live = await broken.forecast(DENVER)
    assert live.available is False and live.items == [] and "503" in (live.reason or "")

v1 hubs and data is shipped and committed. One thing needs you: the GitHub repo creation was blocked by the permission classifier because it creates a public surface, so the two pushes are waiting on it.

**Run this once, then the four commits push:**

```bash
gh repo create ozeriyarin/hubrisk --public --source=C:/ai-projects/hubrisk --remote=origin --push
```

The remote is already configured, so if you prefer to create the repo in the GitHub UI, a plain `git push -u origin main` from the hubrisk folder works too.

**Commits on hubrisk main**
```
b6baae8 feat: v1 hubs and data
cfa6c4e docs: shape v1-hubs-and-data spec
e8f5217 feat: v0 platform lifted under spec
```

**What v1 delivered**
- `config/hubs.yaml`: 15 hubs across the four US Census regions with coordinates, county FIPS and timezone, so "Midwest hubs" is a filter over data.
- `app/data` package: Open-Meteo archive client that verifies units from the response, DuckDB Parquet snapshot writer and store, NWS alerts and forecast client with a per-hub cache that degrades to `available=False` instead of raising, and an ingest with long-backoff retries.
- The committed snapshot covers all 15 hubs for 2016 through 2025 with no nulls. Rows and size are below.
- `agent ingest` command, `ToolContext` handles for v2 and v3, and `/health` now reports data coverage. Verified live on the test server.
- 12 criterion tests. Suite is 89 green, ruff clean.

| Snapshot | Value |
|---|---|
| Rows | 54,795 |
| Parquet size | 346 KB |

**Two findings worth knowing**
- Open-Meteo rate-limits bursts of ten-year requests with 429, so the ingest pauses between hubs and retries with 30-second steps. The full run takes about three minutes.
- Windows has no system timezone database, so `tzdata` was added as a dependency. It is harmless on Render's Linux build.

**Next:** `/shape-spec v2-disruption-kpi`, the scoring engine and its tools.

# Shape Spec

Gather context and structure planning for significant work. **Run this command while in plan mode.**

## Important Guidelines

- **Always use AskUserQuestion tool** when asking the user anything
- **Offer suggestions** — Present options the user can confirm, adjust, or correct
- **Keep it lightweight** — This is shaping, not exhaustive documentation

## Prerequisites

This command **must be run in plan mode**.

**Before proceeding, check if you are currently in plan mode.**

If NOT in plan mode, **stop immediately** and tell the user:

```
Shape-spec must be run in plan mode. Please enter plan mode first, then run /shape-spec again.
```

Do not proceed with any steps below until confirmed to be in plan mode.

## Process

### Step 1: Clarify What We're Building

Use AskUserQuestion to understand the scope:

```
What are we building? Please describe the feature or change.

(Be as specific as you like — I'll ask follow-up questions if needed)
```

Based on their response, ask 1-2 clarifying questions if the scope is unclear. Examples:
- "Is this a new feature or a change to existing functionality?"
- "What's the expected outcome when this is done?"
- "Are there any constraints or requirements I should know about?"

### Step 2: Gather Visuals

Use AskUserQuestion:

```
Do you have any visuals to reference?

- Mockups or wireframes
- Screenshots of similar features
- Examples from other apps

(Paste images, share file paths, or say "none")
```

If visuals are provided, note them for inclusion in the spec folder.

### Step 3: Identify Reference Implementations

Use AskUserQuestion:

```
Is there similar code in this codebase I should reference?

Examples:
- "The comments feature is similar to what we're building"
- "Look at how src/features/notifications/ handles real-time updates"
- "No existing references"

(Point me to files, folders, or features to study)
```

If references are provided, read and analyze them to inform the plan.

### Step 4: Check Product Context

Check if `agent-os/product/` exists and contains files.

If it exists, read key files (like `mission.md`, `roadmap.md`, `tech-stack.md`) and use AskUserQuestion:

```
I found product context in agent-os/product/. Should this feature align with any specific product goals or constraints?

Key points from your product docs:
- [summarize relevant points]

(Confirm alignment or note any adjustments)
```

If no product folder exists, skip this step.

### Step 5: Surface Relevant Standards

Read `agent-os/standards/index.yml` to identify relevant standards based on the feature being built.

Use AskUserQuestion to confirm:

```
Based on what we're building, these standards may apply:

1. **api/response-format** — API response envelope structure
2. **api/error-handling** — Error codes and exception handling
3. **database/migrations** — Migration patterns

Should I include these in the spec? (yes / adjust: remove 3, add frontend/forms)
```

Read the confirmed standards files to include their content in the plan context.

### Step 6: Generate Spec Folder Name

Create a folder name using this format:
```
YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-{feature-slug}/
```

Where:
- Date/time is current timestamp
- Feature slug is derived from the feature description (lowercase, hyphens, max 40 chars)

Example: `2026-01-15-1430-user-comment-system/`

**Note:** If `agent-os/specs/` doesn't exist, create it when saving the spec folder.

### Step 7: Structure the Plan

Now build the plan with **Task 1 always being "Save spec documentation"**.

Present this structure to the user:

```
Here's the plan structure. Task 1 saves all our shaping work before implementation begins.

---

## Task 1: Save Spec Documentation

Create `agent-os/specs/{folder-name}/` with:

- **plan.md** — This full plan
- **shape.md** — Shaping notes (scope, decisions, context from our conversation)
- **standards.md** — Relevant standards that apply to this work
- **references.md** — Pointers to reference implementations studied
- **visuals/** — Any mockups or screenshots provided

## Task 2: [First implementation task]

[Description based on the feature]

## Task 3: [Next task]

...

---

Does this plan structure look right? I'll fill in the implementation tasks next.
```

### Step 8: Complete the Plan

After Task 1 is confirmed, continue building out the remaining implementation tasks based on:
- The feature scope from Step 1
- Patterns from reference implementations (Step 3)
- Constraints from standards (Step 5)

Each task should be specific and actionable.

### Step 9: Ready for Execution

When the full plan is ready:

```
Plan complete. When you approve and execute:

1. Task 1 will save all spec documentation first
2. Then implementation tasks will proceed

Ready to start? (approve / adjust)
```

## Output Structure

The spec folder will contain:

```
agent-os/specs/{YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-feature-slug}/
├── plan.md           # The full plan
├── shape.md          # Shaping decisions and context
├── standards.md      # Which standards apply and key points
├── references.md     # Pointers to similar code
└── visuals/          # Mockups, screenshots (if any)
```

## shape.md Content

The shape.md file should capture:

```markdown
# {Feature Name} — Shaping Notes

## Scope

[What we're building, from Step 1]

## Decisions

- [Key decisions made during shaping]
- [Constraints or requirements noted]

## Context

- **Visuals:** [List of visuals provided, or "None"]
- **References:** [Code references studied]
- **Product alignment:** [Notes from product context, or "N/A"]

## Standards Applied

- api/response-format — [why it applies]
- api/error-handling — [why it applies]
```

## standards.md Content

Include the full content of each relevant standard:

```markdown
# Standards for {Feature Name}

The following standards apply to this work.

---

## api/response-format

[Full content of the standard file]

---

## api/error-handling

[Full content of the standard file]
```

## references.md Content

```markdown
# References for {Feature Name}

## Similar Implementations

### {Reference 1 name}

- **Location:** `src/features/comments/`
- **Relevance:** [Why this is relevant]
- **Key patterns:** [What to borrow from this]

### {Reference 2 name}

...
```

## Tips

- **Keep shaping fast** — Don't over-document. Capture enough to start, refine as you build.
- **Visuals are optional** — Not every feature needs mockups.
- **Standards guide, not dictate** — They inform the plan but aren't always mandatory.
- **Specs are discoverable** — Months later, someone can find this spec and understand what was built and why.
